This relationship is supported by multiple evidence chains, each linking Boric acid to a common intermediate (Aquaporin-1 or Sodium/calcium exchanger 1) that is then targeted by a different compound (Camphor) and finally by the receptor of interest. The consistent involvement of Aquaporin-1 and Camphor in this chain suggests a potential mechanism where the effects of Boric acid are mediated through these intermediaries, possibly by modulating ion transport or other cellular processes. The presence of multiple overlapping targets and the shared pathway highlight a possible functional link between Boric acid and the receptor, though the exact mechanism remains to be elucidated.
